status.d: Minor Industrial is permitted in BE; Major Industrial is not. A large data centre is treated by the City as Major Industrial. A smaller one whose noise, emissions and fuel or battery hazards stay inside the site could be argued as Minor Industrial — the Development Planner decides.

screen.why: Edmonton BE s. 5.2: mechanical and electrical equipment, transformers and cooling towers "must be screened from view from Abutting Streets and Sites in non-industrial Zones" (register arch_ezbLoad). The plant is screened by default; "leave it seen" is not offered here.

notes: Noise: needs the roof cooling plant in an enclosed plant room. On the roof, even with low-noise chillers and a solid screen, it would give about 59 dBA at 8065 CEDRIC MAH ROAD NW (BRH), 98 m away, over the 50 dBA night limit (Bylaw 14600 s. 20(1)). The plant room is the next measure, and the least that passes; its floor comes out of the building (register arch_nz_nswDcNoise).

Noise: needs a plant room: solid walls, roof RW 47 or better, gaps sealed, louvres of at least 6–27 dB by band (NSW 2021 Table 4-5): −25 dB (arch_nz_nswDcNoise). Without it: about 62–65 dBA (quieter–standard unit rating) at the property line of 8065 CEDRIC MAH ROAD NW (BRH), 101 m away; limit 50 dBA at night (Bylaw 14600 s. 20(1)).

s.src: Air-cooled chillers with free-cooling coils (air cooling): an air-cooled hall needs chilled water at about 13 °C or warmer (NREL for DOE FEMP, Best Practices Guide 2024, s. 5.2.1), and a dry cooler cannot cool water below the outdoor air (rated units leave it 3–11 K above), so chillers carry the full load in summer. genLines: 3 generator sets of about 2 MW carry 5.9 MW; with spares, 4. Placed: 0 on the roof, 4 in the yard.
Each about 13.493 × 3.488 m, 4.777 m high; 1.5 m from the building, 2 m between sets (1 m clear all round, CSA C282 6.5.1.1; register arch_csa_c282).

Fuel in each set's sub-base tank: about 6200 L. In the yard: 3 m from the property line and 1.5 m from the building (CSA B139.1.0 Table 2; register arch_csa_b139). On a roof: at most 1,250 L a tank and 2,500 L a supply line (B139.1.1 6.5.3). FM 5-32 (insurer guidance, not law): not on the roof or in a basement.

base.rule: Height is measured from Grade, a geodetic elevation the Development Planner sets by one of three methods (corners of the site, front-yard corners on steep residential lots, or the rear lot line corners for a building facing an alley) or an alternative method (Bylaw 20001 s. 5.70.2, pp. 826–828; 'Grade' p. 1036). Which method applies is not known, so the lot grade shown is not the base (?).
